title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes concern the structure at infinity of the moduli multiplicities M_{g,ν}. Y is a smooth compact multiplicity, an orbifold or stack such as the Deligne–Mumford compactification, with a normal-crossings divisor Θ at infinity and open part Y* = Y \ Θ. The closed strata of Θ are taken in normalized form D' → Y. Because components of Θ can self-intersect, these maps are only local immersions, not embeddings. The previous page drew such a curve with a double point and explained that the 'tubular neighbourhood' must be taken 'upstairs': as a germ of manifold around D' (unique up to unique isomorphism), not as an open subset of Y.

This page.
(1) Grothendieck suggests a direct, purely topological (topos-theoretic) definition. It should be valid, 'sauf erreur', whenever one has a local immersion of topoi. The tubular neighbourhood V_{D',Y} is the germ of topos attached to the local immersion D' → Y. In modern terms it is the germ of the 'unfolded' neighbourhood: an étalé neighbourhood of D' over Y, in which the branches through a self-crossing are separated.
(2) Functoriality. For a composite of local immersions D'' → D' → Y (deeper stratum inside a shallower one) there are canonical commutative diagrams (235): D'' → D' over V_{D'',Y} → V_{D',Y} → Y, with both bottom maps local immersions. The sketch shows a band V_{D'} around D', with small hatched discs V_{D''} around the points of D'' (the case where D' is a curve and D'' a set of points).
(3) He brings in Θ. Pulling back Y* gives V*_{D',Y} = V_{D',Y} \ Θ_{D',Y} and V*_{D'',Y}. These are the punctured or deleted tubular neighbourhoods. The next page notes that each is again a normal-crossings complement inside a tubular neighbourhood.

Purpose (next page, (237)). The aim is to obtain maps of fundamental groupoids Π_1 V*_{D'',Y} → Π_1 V*_{D',Y}. These groupoids are taken with 'sub-domains and isomorphisms between them' as base objects rather than points. The result is a coherent system of local fundamental groupoids at infinity, functorial in the poset or category of strata. This system is what the 'structure à l'infini' of the Teichmüller tower is built from: the inertia/boundary subgroups and how they glue.
errors: No substantive errors visible. The direct topos-theoretic definition is only asserted ('sauf erreur'), not carried out.

The germ-level functoriality is not checked: maps between germs are only defined after shrinking. Canonicity of (235) needs uniqueness up to unique isomorphism, which is stated on the previous page for the differentiable case but not proved for topoi.
Equation numbering: the diagram is labelled (235), not (2.35); compare (236) and (237) on the next page.

ideas.what: Tubular neighbourhood of a non-embedded local immersion (normalized stratum mapping to Y), defined as a germ unique up to unique isomorphism. It is defined in differentiable, topological and topos-theoretic frameworks.
ideas.modern_name: germ of étalé tubular neighbourhood / neighbourhood of a stratum in a normal-crossings compactification, with self-intersections unfolded
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical in differential topology (tubular neighbourhoods of immersions). The topos/germ version is related to later work on tubular neighbourhoods in étale homotopy (Fujiwara, Ayoub) and to homotopy links (Quinn).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν} and 'tubular neighbourhoods' of the boundary only informally; unsure about any precise definition.

ideas.what: Functoriality of tubular neighbourhoods for composites of local immersions D'' → D' → Y, giving canonical diagrams relating neighbourhoods of deeper and shallower strata.
ideas.modern_name: functor from the category of strata (with local immersions) to germs of spaces; a precursor of stratified homotopy / exit-path data
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit-path ∞-categories); Barwick–Glasman–Haine (exodromy). In the moduli setting: Ihara–Nakamura and Nakamura (fundamental groups at infinity), Boggi.
ideas.where_published: Spirit of the Esquisse ('tour de Teichmüller', gluing of boundary groups); no precise published statement known to me.

ideas.what: Deleted tubular neighbourhoods V* = V \ Θ of boundary strata, used to define local fundamental groupoids at infinity and the maps between them.
ideas.modern_name: punctured tubular neighbourhood / homotopy link of a boundary stratum; local fundamental groups at infinity of M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Nakamura (1997, tangential base points and Teichmüller groups at infinity); Nakamura; Boggi; Harvey (curve complex)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a direct definition of the tubular-neighbourhood germ V_{D',Y} for any local immersion of topoi, with canonical functoriality for composites. He does not carry it out on this page. A general topos-theoretic 'germ of tubular neighbourhood' for local immersions, with the deleted version V \ Θ, is not standard in the literature as such.
missed.quote: une définition directe, dans un style encore plus topologique, valable chaque fois ... (s.f. erreur) ... une immersion locale de topos
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give an intrinsic, topos-level construction of the 'homotopy link' data of a normal-crossings boundary. This is relevant to stratified homotopy theory and exodromy, and to the profinite or étale Teichmüller tower at infinity.

missed.claim: The functorial system of deleted neighbourhoods and their fundamental groupoids, indexed by composites of local immersions of strata, anticipates exit-path / stratified-homotopy descriptions of the boundary of M_{g,n}. Here it is formulated with non-embedded (normalized) strata.
missed.quote: Il a des propriétés de fonctorialité telles, que l'on trouve, partant d'une composé d'immersions locales D''→D'→Y, des diagrammes commutatifs canoniques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precursor formulation linking Grothendieck–Teichmüller/Lego ideas to later exodromy and stratified homotopy frameworks. It is mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a careful, functorial notion of tubular and deleted neighbourhoods of normalized boundary strata, intended as a topos-theoretic definition. This is a natural unpublished technical detail behind the Esquisse's 'structure at infinity'. Its substance has been rediscovered in other forms (Ihara–Nakamura, exit paths), so it is notable but not startling.
transcription_corrections: The diagram label is '(235)' (consistent with (236) and (237) on the next page), not '(2.35)'. The '(235)' next to the figure is crossed out.
Line 3 is largely illegible; the sense is probably 'valable chaque fois qu'on a (sauf erreur) ... une immersion locale de topos'.
'Nous [?] considérons' appears to read 'Nous [struck word] considérons maintenant'.
